parameters.description: Filter resources by event-type. Accepts a comma-separated list, and a webhook must subscribe to every listed event-type to match (AND semantics). A single webhook can subscribe to multiple event-types. Values must be event-types returned by `GET /core/webhooks/event-types`.

parameters.description: Filter resources by URL. The value is matched as a case-insensitive substring, not as a glob pattern, so `example.com` matches `https://example.com/hook`.

get.description: Retrieves all webhook entries for a tenant that the user has access to. Users assigned the `TenantAdmin` role can retrieve all webhooks of the tenant; other users only retrieve the webhooks they own. Values of `encryptedHeaders` are never returned, only their header names.

201.description: The webhook was created. The response contains the stored webhook, where `secret` is replaced by `secretKeyAdded` and `encryptedHeaders` is returned as a list of header names.

403.description: The request is not allowed, for example because the user lacks the required permissions, the target URL is forbidden, the event-type is not enabled for the tenant, or the user's 150-webhook quota is reached.

post.description: Creates a new webhook. User must be assigned the `TenantAdmin` role to create `tenant` level webhooks. Each user can own up to 150 webhooks per tenant; creating a webhook beyond that quota is rejected with `403`.

get.description: Returns details for a specific webhook.

patch.description: Updates one or more individual properties of a webhook using a JSON Patch document, leaving all other properties unchanged. The patch is applied to the stored webhook and the result is validated as a whole, so a patch that produces an invalid webhook is rejected. When `/url` is changed on a webhook that has encrypted headers, every existing encrypted header must also be replaced or removed in the same patch, otherwise the request is rejected with `400`. Changing read-only properties is rejected with `409`, and changing `/ownerId` requires permission to transfer ownership.

put.description: Replaces all writable properties of a webhook and returns the updated webhook. This is a full replacement: every writable property that is omitted from the request body is reset to its default, so omitting `secret`, `encryptedHeaders`, `headers` or `filter` clears them, and omitting `enabled` disables the webhook. Because `secret` is never returned and `encryptedHeaders` is returned as a list of header names, a `GET` response cannot be sent back unchanged as a `PUT` request body; re-send those values explicitly, and use `PATCH` to change individual properties. Read-only properties such as `id`, `createdAt`, `createdByUserId` and `origin` cannot be changed and are rejected with `409`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of deliveries to retrieve

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by, prefix with -/+ to indicate order

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter resources by status (success or fail)

get.description: Returns deliveries for a specific webhook. Delivery history is stored for 1 week.
Returns details for a specific delivery.

201.description: A new delivery was created for the resend attempt. Check `status` to see whether the delivery itself succeeded or failed.

403.description: The request is not allowed, for example because the user lacks the required permissions or the event-type of the delivery is not enabled for the tenant.

post.description: Resends the event payload of an existing delivery and returns the new delivery. The event payload is taken from the original delivery, but the webhook's current configuration (URL, headers, secret and certificate settings) is used to send it. The resend is attempted synchronously and a new delivery record is always created, so a `201` response can contain a delivery with status `fail`. A resend is subject to the same validation and failure handling as an automatic delivery, so a webhook that is no longer valid or that exceeds the delivery failure threshold can be disabled as a result.

filter.description:
Filter that should match for a webhook to be triggered.
Supported common attribute names are 'id', 'spaceId' and 'topLevelResourceId'. Individual event-types can support additional event-specific attributes, which cannot be combined with other event-types in the same webhook. For example "com.qlik.v1.app.reload.finished" supports "data.status" with the allowed values "SUCCEEDED", "FAILED", "CANCELED" and "EXCEEDED_LIMIT".
The authoritative set of filterable attributes and their allowed values for each event-type is returned in the `allowedFilters` property of `GET /core/webhooks/event-types`.
Supported attribute operators are 'eq' and 'ne'.
Supported logical operators are 'and' and 'or'.
Note that attribute values must be valid JSON strings, hence they're enclosed with double quotes.
For more detailed information regarding the SCIM filter syntax (RFC7644) used please follow the link to external documentation.

secret.description: Shared secret used to sign the webhook delivery. Each delivery is sent with a `Qlik-Signature` header containing the hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, computed with this secret, so the receiver can verify that the payload is genuine and unmodified. The secret is stored encrypted and is never returned by the API; responses report only `secretKeyAdded`.

encryptedHeaders.description: Headers that are persisted encrypted and decrypted again to be sent as normal headers in the post request (webhook delivery). In requests they are supplied as name/value pairs, but responses return only the header names as a list of strings, because the values are never disclosed. If the URL changes, these headers must be re-entered. Note: duplicate headers are not allowed and are case-insensitive. Maximum combined size: 2048 bytes (total of all encrypted header names and values).

enableCloudEventDelivery.description: Whether this webhook delivers events as CloudEvents. On creation, the service determines the effective value from tenant feature flags and webhook origin; the supplied value is not authoritative. On PUT, omission is treated as false. When feature flags are enabled, the service may automatically enable this for exclusive Data Integration webhooks. Once enabled, it cannot be disabled; omitting it when replacing an enabled webhook therefore returns `403`.

path.description: The path of the webhook property to patch. Only writable properties can be patched; read-only properties such as `/id`, `/createdAt`, `/createdByUserId` and `/origin` are rejected. Individual members of `/headers` and `/encryptedHeaders` can also be addressed directly, for example `/encryptedHeaders/myHeader`.

value.description: The value to be used for this operation. The type must match the patched property, for example an array of event-type names for `/eventTypes` or an object of header name/value pairs for `/headers`. Not used by the `remove` operation.
